author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing answers a page below the first with the first page
summary: Asking the owner listing for a page before the first returns the first page of owners and succeeds, instead of showing the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner listing naming a page below the first, when the listing is opened, then the first page of owners is shown
given that same request, when the listing is opened, then it succeeds rather than showing the error page
given a page of zero and any negative page, when each is requested, then both yield the first page of owners
non_goals: a page past the last page
a page value that is not a number
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at line 1; decisions array is empty, so the request as stated bounds the scope. No Non-Goals row is touched, so no scope_overrides. The three slice non-goals are unstated by the owner, not declined by them - recorded as the open question 'How far does tolerant paging reach?' in docs/prd.md. PRD edits: new requirement in the Owner records narrative, two Done-when bullets, edge case 4.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: No new type, package, or pattern. The slice adds one input-normalization step to the existing owner-listing path in OwnerController, which system-design.md Contracts already names as the owner search-with-paging surface. Diagnosed cause (read directly from source, no IDE oracle connected): OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName converts the one-based page parameter to a zero-based index with 'page - 1' and hands it to PageRequest.of, which rejects a negative index with IllegalArgumentException. src/main/java holds no @ControllerAdvice, @ExceptionHandler, or ErrorController, so the exception reaches Spring Boot default error handling and renders the error page. Binding is not the cause: @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page binds 0 and negative values without complaint.
integration_points: processFindForm publishes currentPage into the model; templates/owners/ownersList.html drives the current-page marker and the first/previous/next/last links from that value
findPaginatedForOwnersLastName is the only caller of PageRequest.of on the owner path

patterns.description: processFindForm - clamp here. Normalize once into a local (for example int pageNumber = Math.max(page, 1)) and pass that value to BOTH findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel. Clamping inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName instead would fetch the right rows but leave currentPage at 0 in the model: the template would mark no page as current and would render 'next' pointing at ?page=1, the page already on screen. One normalization site keeps query and model in agreement.

processFindFormSuccess is the MockMvc stub shape to copy for both new tests. Stub findByLastNameStartingWith with a PageImpl holding MORE THAN ONE owner: processFindForm redirects to the owner detail when getTotalElements() == 1, and returns findOwners with a 'notFound' rejection when the page is empty. Only a multi-owner page reaches the owners/ownersList view the acceptance criteria name.

risks.risk: A reviewer reads the clamp as a business rule in a web controller, which architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog forbids adding.
risks.mitigation: Design ruling: this is request-binding adaptation, not a business rule. A page number is a presentation concept - it appears in no domain type, and page size is a controller-local variable. Coercing an out-of-range query parameter into the paging port's valid domain is the 'binds the request' half of the Web controller row.

risks.risk: A reviewer reads the clamp as masking a failure, against Design Principle 7 (fail secure).
risks.mitigation: Design ruling: REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 defines a page below the first as MEANING the first page, so this is not an error path being defaulted. The request is a read-only GET, so no partially-applied write can survive and no message content changes.

risks.risk: VetController.findPaginated carries the identical 'page - 1' shape and the identical failure, so after this slice the two listings answer a page below the first differently.
risks.mitigation: Leave VetController untouched. The prd-entry lists the veterinarian directory as a non-goal and docs/prd.md records the reach of tolerant paging as an open question. Do not extract a shared pagination helper in this slice.

notes: Durable-memory write: docs/system-design.md Contracts table, OwnerController row - purpose gains the normalization guarantee and Implements gains REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001. No ADR: the tolerate-versus-reject choice is a product decision already settled in the PRD, and the placement follows an existing pattern rather than departing from one. No new vocabulary - docs/ubiquitous-language.md carries no page or listing term, and none is needed. Autofix audit: the handoff log holds no design-doc-autofix records. Out of scope for the implementer, per the prd-entry non-goals: a page past the last page (still falls into the existing empty-result 'not found' branch), a non-numeric page value (still a binding failure), and the vet listing.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: No NVD match was run in this review: build.gradle configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin, so dependencyCheckAnalyze does not exist and the reviewer has no network access. Resolved framework baseline read from build.gradle is Spring Boot 4.1.0 with io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7 — unverified against the NVD, to be closed by CI or a human. This is a standing project gap, not a defect of this change, which alters no dependency declaration

Out of scope for this requirement and already recorded in prd.md Open Questions: a non-numeric page value still fails type binding and reaches the error page, which renders the exception message. Worth a future slice if that message is ever judged to leak internal detail
approved_aspects: Threat-model walk over the full diff finds no row of docs/security-principles.md § Realization introduced: no query text is concatenated (findByLastNameStartingWith stays a derived query with a Pageable), no new endpoint or management exposure, no request-derived value composes a path or resource name, no deserialization surface, no credential added or logged, and no dependency declaration changed

Math.max(page, 1) in OwnerController.processFindForm strictly narrows the request-derived value reaching PageRequest.of and the model, so the change moves the application toward the baseline rather than away from it

The clamp removes a request-triggered error-page path: page<=0 previously reached PageRequest.of(page-1, 5) and surfaced IllegalArgumentException, which docs/system-design.md § Security Context records as rendering the underlying exception message to the reader. One attacker-reachable exception-message disclosure is closed and none is opened

Normalizing before both call sites (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) keeps currentPage in the model consistent with the queried page. ownersList.html feeds currentPage into Thymeleaf preprocessing (@{'/owners?page=__${currentPage - 1}__'}); the clamp shrinks the value domain reaching that expression to positive ints and introduces no new value there. The parameter is bound as int, so non-numeric text fails binding before reaching the expression

No integer overflow reachable: pageNumber >= 1 by construction, so pageNumber - 1 cannot underflow, and Spring's PageRequest widens the offset to long. Page size stays the fixed literal 5, so no request-derived value controls allocation size
No new class of unbounded work: a very large page value was already accepted before this change and still resolves to an empty page and the findOwners view, so resource exposure is unchanged

Test-only fix delta since round 1 (the two duplicate tests collapsed into one @ParameterizedTest over {0, -3}) adds no production surface; junit-jupiter-params arrives transitively through the already-declared spring-boot-starter-test, so no dependency was added and the four Adding a New Dependency checks do not engage

Detection-pattern sweeps over the diff: no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, no Files/FileWriter/FileOutputStream, no enableDefaultTyping/@JsonTypeInfo, no /tmp/ path, no System.out/err, no string-concatenated log or query, no secret-shaped literal (token, password, secret, key) in any of the four changed files

Class sweep for the clamp's category (request-derived numeric reaching a paging/index API in a controller): OwnerController is the only controller in src/main/java taking a page @RequestParam, so no second unclamped instance exists to fix
Concurrency: the added state is a method-local int in a singleton controller, introducing no shared mutable state

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner-listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: Four files in one module, no sensitive paths, no dependency or config change: three effective production lines inside OwnerController.processFindForm plus one parameterized test and two purpose-level doc edits, and the only behavior reached is the owner listing's paging path.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do exactly what the diff advertises. Math.max(page, 1) narrows the value domain, both former uses of the raw page parameter (in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) are switched to the clamped local with no stale use left behind, so query and model cannot diverge, and a pageNumber of at least 1 makes the pageNumber-minus-1 index non-negative with no overflow and no new branch.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized test over 0 and -3 falsifies both real failure modes rather than restating the code: with no clamp PageRequest.of(-1, 5) throws and the isOk assertion fails, and with the clamp misplaced inside the repository call the currentPage-equals-1 model assertion fails; the two-owner stub is deliberately chosen so the assertions land on the ownersList view instead of the single-result redirect.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved round 2 with empty findings and the planned roster of three was fully answered, but the security-reviewer's late-round approval parks two recommendations: no NVD dependency scan was run because the project configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin, and a non-numeric page value still reaches the error page, which renders the exception message.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions, and the diff lands exactly on the two file targets the prd-entry named; the identical page-minus-1 shape in VetController is left untouched as a recorded non-goal, with the reach of tolerant paging written up as an open question rather than silently widened.

rationale: The clamp reads clean on every axis and the test genuinely falsifies the defect. What wants a human glance is the security reviewer's two parked items: the project runs no dependency scan at all, and a non-numeric page still leaks an exception message to the error page. Neither is caused by this change; both outlive it.
